evidence: letsencrypt-key-and-bundle: ssl_base.pp:70-76 set key_file ${ssl_private_dir}/${myprefix}-key.pem and bundle_file ${ssl_certs_dir}/${myprefix}.${myservice}.bundle.pem from <prefix>.pem then <prefix>-chain.pem; with the letsencrypt fixture (p8test, nginx, true) the probe reads /etc/ssl/private/p8test-key.pem (0600 root:root from 85-92 defaults), >=2 certificates in /etc/ssl/certs/p8test.nginx.bundle.pem, and the key matching the first certificate (the leaf, order 01); the mismatch compares the second (chain) certificate's public key, which must change the verdict

the-bundle-is-the-leaf-then-its-issuer: ssl_base.pp:109-119 concat fragments order 01 = <prefix>.crt, 02 = <prefix>.intermediate.crt into the bundle (0644 from 100-107); master_fixtures.sh lays server.crt (CN p8test.invalid) as ssl/p8test.crt and ca.crt (CN p8test throwaway CA) as ssl/p8test.intermediate.crt, so 2 certificates, leaf CN then CA CN, and verify OK is exactly what the code produces; the mismatch swaps only the trust anchor for the system CA bundle, which did not sign the leaf, so the verdict must change

other-owners-and-groups: ssl_base.pp:85-92 owner => $owner, group => $group, mode 0600 on the key (and 100-107 the same owner/group with 0644 on the bundle); the owners fixture sets www-data/www-data, so www-data:www-data 600 and 644 is what the code declares
